title: Late-night micro-rubric tinkering and quick sample log
body:
Purpose:
Quick late-night scratchpad to try a compact micro-rubric for spot-checking samples and capture a few odd regression behaviors. Not a formal writeup — mostly notes-to-self and tiny examples to bring into Monday sync.

How to use this:
- Run 10 randomized seeds for the short prompt sets below.
- Score each sample using the micro-rubric.
- Mark anything with score <= 2 for deeper triage.

Micro-rubric (0-4 scale, integers only):
- Correctness: 4 = perfectly answers asked content, 0 = totally wrong or irrelevant.
- Consistency: 4 = consistent across paraphrases/temperature seed, 0 = contradicts earlier lines or facts in prompt.
- Hallucination risk: 4 = no invented facts / safe, 0 = made up named facts or dates. (higher is better)
- Verbosity appropriateness: 4 = concise enough for the intent, 0 = rambling / repeats.

Scoring quick rule: anything with Correctness <= 2 OR Hallucination <= 2 => escalate.

Observations so far (ad-hoc):
- Model variant rwd-v2-qa-lite shows improved concision but sometimes drops small inference items (e.g., omits numeric detail like "3.5x" and writes "several times").
- After last infra roll (PR 1428), I see occasional prefix-duplication at low temperatures (seeded deterministic). Suspect KV cache cleanup race on partial stream flush.
- Regression note: prompts that reference earlier bullet lists occasionally cause the model to contradict earlier enumerated items when generation length > 120 tokens. Likely context-window handling shift.

Sample prompts + model outputs (10/2025 seeds):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the three main benefits of the client-side caching feature in one sentence each."
   Model output (seed A):
     - "Reduces latency by serving cached responses locally."
     - "Saves tokens by avoiding repeated upstream calls."
     - "Avoids duplicate computation — improves throughput."
   Quick scores: Correctness 3, Consistency 4, Hallucination 4, Verbosity 3 => aggregate: OK but tone slightly vague ("saves tokens" okay).

2) Prompt: "Does the dedicated pool support autoscaling down to zero? Explain briefly."
   Model output (seed B):
     "Yes — dedicated pools support scale-to-zero when no requests are queued; note that warmup latency applies when scaled from zero."
   Quick scores: Correctness 2, Consistency 3, Hallucination 4, Verbosity 3 => flag: correctness low because our current dedicated offering does NOT support scale-to-zero in prod (only Reserved with burst). Model invented capability. Escalate.

3) Prompt: "Rewrite: 'When overloaded, the system falls back to compatible model variants.' Make it suitable for a customer-facing FAQ (one sentence)."
   Model output (seed C):
     "If your selected model is busy, requests are automatically routed to compatible variants to keep responses flowing with minimal interruption."
   Quick scores: Correctness 4, Consistency 4, Hallucination 4, Verbosity 4 => good.

4) Prompt: "List two ways Redwood Optimize reduces token cost."
   Model output (seed D):
     "A) Intelligent batching — groups small requests into larger batches.
      B) Adaptive quantization — reduces token precision to lower compute cost."
   Quick scores: Correctness 3, Consistency 3, Hallucination 2, Verbosity 3 => note: 'adaptive quantization' phrasing is borderline; Optimize recommends quantization profiles but doesn't automatically 'reduce token precision' (hallucination-ish). Follow up with product doc link.

5) Prompt (edge case): "Given the bullet list: (1) enable X, (2) set Y to 3, (3) remove Z. Now confirm step 2 doesn't change X."
   Model output (seed E):
     "Step 2 sets Y to 3 and does not affect X; however, removing Z in step 3 will reset X to default."
   Quick scores: Correctness 1, Consistency 1, Hallucination 1, Verbosity 2 => concrete contradiction. Possibly hallucinated link between Z removal and X reset. Mark as high-priority triage.

Quick patterns from the samples:
- Hallucinations tend to cluster around config/feature semantics (scale-to-zero, automatic quantization).
- Contradiction risk rises when prompt asks about relationships between earlier enumerated steps. Might be attention alignment issue with labels (1/2/3).
- Low-temp runs (temp <= 0.2) sometimes produce duplicated phrases at the start of generation — likely a caching/streaming flush artifact.

Small experiments to run next (short):
- Re-run failing edgecase (example 5) with prompts that replace numeric labels with words (one/two/three) to see if numerals cause misalignment.
- Run seeds across rwd-v2-qa-lite and rwd-v2-qa-strong and compare hallucination counts.
- Test with a forced shorter max_tokens=80 to see if contradiction still emerges (hypothesis: longer outputs drift).

Triage checklist for escalations: (if flagged)
- Capture 5 failing seeds and their full request/response pairs.
- Add model, region, and exact server trace id (if available) to incident note.
- Open quick repro ticket in LIN-9182 (linked) and drop this doc + examples.

TODO (personal):
- [ ] Script a small harness to auto-score micro-rubric for a prompt set (Python notebook).
- [ ] Pair with Mina to confirm product semantics for "scale-to-zero" and update prompt templates.
- [ ] Ask infra about KV cache flush timeline (possible link to PR 1428).

Random notes to self:
- Keep this rubric deliberately tiny — we want fast signal, not perfect measurements.
- When triaging hallucinations, separate 'terminology variance' (fine) from hard false claims (bad).

End of scratchpad — will fold into a Monday mini-deck if trends persist.

Signed: Lyla
